details: Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) experienced over $1.2 billion in net outflows last week, with Blackrock's IBIT leading with a $1 billion outflow. This significant shift in institutional sentiment saw capital simultaneously flowing into XRP, Solana, and HYPE-linked products, suggesting a rotation into alternative crypto narratives.
title: Bitcoin ETFs See Over $1.2B Outflows as Institutional Sentiment Shifts

details: Mastercard Transaction Services (U.S.) LLC received a Virtual Currency License from the New York State Department of Financial Services on May 27, 2026. This regulatory approval allows Mastercard to expand its stablecoin and tokenized digital payment infrastructure within New York, building on its $1.8 billion acquisition of stablecoin firm BVNK in March 2026.
title: Mastercard Secures New York BitLicense to Advance Stablecoin and Digital Payments

details: Nathan Allman, the founder and CEO of Ondo Finance, a notable figure in the tokenized real-world assets (RWA) sector, passed away unexpectedly at the age of 35. The cause of death was not disclosed. Ian De Bode, Ondo's longtime President, has been named CEO.
title: Ondo Finance CEO Nathan Allman Dies Unexpectedly at 35

details: Bitcoin's price dropped below $75,000, showing a decoupling from a strong stock market buoyed by the AI boom. This decline is attributed to Bitcoin miners increasingly shifting their focus towards AI infrastructure and persistent delays in key US regulatory acts that aim to provide clarity for crypto taxation.
title: Bitcoin Falls as Miners Pivot to AI, Pro-Crypto Legislation Stalls

details: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has taken the unusual step of requesting a federal court to nullify a $5 million settlement it previously reached with the cryptocurrency exchange Gemini. This action by the CFTC indicates a potential shift in its regulatory approach.
title: CFTC Seeks to Void $5M Gemini Settlement, Signaling Regulatory Pivot
